I've been working this land since I was 18, so I know what works here in Quzhou. The North China Plain has its rhythms — winter wheat going in October, summer maize right after harvest in June. My 10 mu runs as a full rotation; the same fields carry both crops year-round. My son's off-farm income gives us some financial cushion, so I don't have to cut corners on inputs, but I'm not wasteful either.

**Wheat:** I'll plant an improved variety — something in the Jimai line that the county extension has been pushing, good resistance to powdery mildew and fusarium which we've had trouble with. I'll do rotary tillage before sowing, incorporate the base fertilizer, then topdress nitrogen at jointing when I can actually see how the stand looks. Three irrigations: one at sowing if the soil is dry (越冬水 if needed), one at jointing (拔节水), one at heading (抽穗水). That's standard here and the well can handle it. Two pesticide passes — herbicide early on, fungicide around booting. I expect around 450 kg/mu which is solid for our conditions.

**Maize:** Right after wheat harvest I go straight to no-till seeding — saves time and moisture, and the soil structure is fine. I use a hybrid, Zhengdan 958 or similar, proven in this county. Maize is more rain-fed in summer but I'll irrigate twice — once around silking if it's dry, once at grain fill. Fertilizer is heavier on nitrogen but split: base at seeding, side-dress at V6. One or two pesticide passes depending on aphid and bollworm pressure. Targeting 580 kg/mu.
